**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/28 (Sun) 01:40
- [USER] User inquired about the differences between marriage and a civil union.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Marriage is a legally recognized union between two people, typically recognized at the federal level in the United States and most other countries.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Marriage grants couples a wide range of legal rights and benefits, including inheritance rights, tax benefits, and the ability to make medical decisions for one another.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Marriage can be performed by a religious official or by a government official.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] A civil union is a legally recognized relationship that grants couples some, but not all, of the rights and benefits of marriage.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Civil unions are typically created at the state level and are not recognized by the federal government.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Civil unions may not provide the same level of legal rights as marriage, such as Social Security benefits, immigration rights, or the ability to file joint tax returns.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Some states or countries may offer civil unions as an alternative to marriage for same-sex couples, while others may only offer civil unions and not allow same-sex marriage.
